title: Fix the Bug: Computed Property Setter
hints: A get/set pair should round-trip: set a value, read it back, get the same number.
The getter computes `allowed - taken`. Solve that for `allowed` when you want `remaining == newValue`.
jsBridge: Computed properties with `get`/`set` are JS getters/setters (`get vacationRemaining() {}`). In the setter, `newValue` is implicit. The bug here is the round-trip rule: setting then getting must return what you set.

compass.q: JS `get x()` / `set x(v)` vs Swift `var x { get set }`: what's `newValue`, and can you rename it?
Computed property vs method: when does something with side effects stop being a property?
Can a computed property be `mutating` in a struct getter? What about `nonmutating set`?
How would you unit test the "set then get returns the same value" law?
